text:
Maria Chen: FYI incoming escalation — customer on paid plan hitting 400s from /v1/tools/run when they pass a file path in tool args. Error: \"Invalid JSON in tool arguments\". They pasted from Windows and I can repro locally.

Ashok Patel: Can you paste the exact payload you sent?

Maria Chen: pasted below (client is an internal CLI wrapper). Note the single quotes and CRLFs they pasted from a Windows editor:

```json
{
  'tool': 'ocr',
  'args': {
    "path": "C:\\Users\\alice\\Downloads\\invoice.pdf",
    "page": 1,
  },
}
```

Maria Chen: Server returns 400 with this body: \"\"{\"error\":\"tool args: malformed JSON: trailing comma at line 7\"}\"\" (from our request-validate step).

support-bot: log snippet from validation service:
```
2026-03-17T12:03:05Z validate: schema error: trailing comma detected at offset 124
request_id=01G8X4M0
payload="{\n  'tool': 'ocr',\n  'args': {\n    \"path\": \"C:\\Users\\alice\\Downloads\\invoice.pdf\",\n    \"page\": 1,\n  },\n}"
```

Ben R.: Looks like two issues: (1) client used single quotes (invalid JSON), (2) Windows path with backslashes is OK if properly escaped but they pasted raw backslashes. The trailing commas break the parser. Do we have telemetry on how often customers paste Windows paths into tool args?

QA Bot: repro note: I reproduced with a small Node script that calls fetch('/v1/tools/run') sending the payload as a raw string with single quotes — server rejects before function selection. Suggestion: Add a preprocessing sanitizer that (a) converts single quotes to double where safe, (b) removes trailing commas in objects/arrays, (c) normalizes CRLF to LF. We should be careful — aggressive fixes can change intended JSON.

Ashok Patel: Agreed, we can't silently mutate arbitrary JSON. But we can implement a lenient parse path for toolargs that attempts a safe normalization when the content-type is application/json and parsing fails. If normalization succeeds and re-parsed value is an object with only string/number/boolean/null/array/object primitives (no executable content), accept it and log a warning + increment a metric. This will reduce support friction for obvious paste errors.

Maria Chen: Customer wants immediate workaround. I told them to run `node -e \"console.log(JSON.stringify(require('./payload.json')))\`` after saving with proper quotes — but they're not comfortable editing. Can we provide a support-side quick fix?

Ben R.: Short term: add a request-level sanitizer that only strips trailing commas and converts CRLF -> LF and attempts to replace balanced single-quoted property names/strings with double quotes. Keep it minimal: if any step fails or the normalized string still fails JSON.parse, return 400. Log normalized and original for audit. Put feature behind a feature flag + opt-in for enterprise workspaces.

QA Bot: I created a minimal repro script and a unit test. Patch idea: https://git.local/redwood/runtime/pulls/4320 (draft). It tries a single safe normalization pass via regex rather than an eval. Tests: windows-paths, trailing-commas, single-quote-strings, and ensure injections are rejected.

Ashok Patel: Risk assessment quick notes: - Benefit: fewer support tickets for paste errors. - Risk: normalization could mask client bugs or alter semantic payloads. Mitigation: limit to toolargs parsing only, metrics + logging + canary (5% incoming hosted API), and require opt-in for Dedicated/Private until validated.

Maria Chen: Customer asked for credit for today while we triage. Case ID CASE-2026-1147. Support suggests 24h usage credit once fix is rolled to canary.

Ben R.: Action items
- Ashok: prepare canary patch with feature flag + metrics (owner: @ashok)
- QA Bot: expand unit tests + fuzz for edge cases (owner: @qa-bot)
- Maria: respond to customer with reproducible workaround (escape backslashes OR attach args as base64) and offer 24h credit pending fix (owner: @maria)

Maria Chen: assigning and updating the case. I'll ping infra/eng-runtime if we see any more regressions. :white_check_mark:

Ashok Patel: I'll open rollout ticket and schedule a small canary tonight. Will post PR link once ready. :rocket:
